1.1.text:
Article 30
The Regency Government and community shall organize Early Childhood Education (PAUD).
Paragraph 3 Employment Article 31 Employers are prohibited from employing Children.
Article 32 (1) The provisions as referred to in Article 31 may be exempted for Children aged between 13 (thirteen) years up to 15 (fifteen) years, to perform light work as long as it does not interfere with physical, mental, and social development and health.
(2) Employers who employ Children in light work as referred to in paragraph (1) must fulfill requirements including: a. written permission from parents or guardian;
b. work agreement between employer and parents or guardian; c. maximum working time of 3 (three) hours;
d. conducted during daytime and does not interfere with school time; e. occupational safety and health;
f. clear employment relationship; and
g. receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The provisions as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, letter b, letter f, and letter g are exempted for Children who work in family businesses.
Article 33 In the event that a company employs Children as referred to in Article 32, then the workplace for Children must be separated from the workplace of adult workers.
Article 34 (1) Children may perform work in a workplace that is part of an educational curriculum or training validated by the authorized official.
(2) Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be at least 14 (fourteen) years of age.

CHAPTER VIII
CHILD PARTICIPATION
Article 55 (1) Every Child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, and thoughts related to life based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
(2) Child Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted through Child Forums starting from the village level, sub-district level within the regency.
(3) Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) represent Children, both in terms of geographical domicile representation, socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.
(4) The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be facilitated by the Regency Government.
(5) The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
Article 56 (1) In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regency Government shall consider and accommodate Children's Opinions submitted through Child Forums.
(2) The Regency Government shall include representatives of Child Forums in the Regency Development Planning Deliberation.

Part Five
Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services Article 51 (1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.
(2) Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) The Regency Government shall implement repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER X
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts development and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
(2) Development as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. training for government apparatus and law enforcers regarding prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent in conducting development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.
Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obligated to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.
(2) The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
(2) The results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of Women and Children protection programs in the Regency.

I,
Article 49 (1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services constitute actions by law enforcement officials provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.
(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
Article 50 (1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 49 are intended to provide accompaniment and protection to Women and Children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty of rights.
(2) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of BAP; b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.
(3) The Regency Government shall provide legal assistance to Children and Women victims of violence free of charge.
(4) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regency Government may cooperate with:
a. Legal Aid Institute (LBH);
b. Women Crisis Center (WCC);
c. Advocates; and/or
d. other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Women are guaranteed the right to obtain education at every level of formal and non-formal education.

Part Two
Community Article 10 (1) The community is obligated and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:
a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervising the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
(2) The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Part Two
Community Article 14 (1) Efforts undertaken by the community in order to prevent violations of Women's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may give rise to violations of Women's rights; b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of unregistered marriages/siri marriages. (2) Efforts undertaken in order to prevent violations of Children's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that give rise to violations of Children's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of marriage at the age of Children.

Paragraph 1
General Article 16 The Regency Government organizes the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of Women's protection.
Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters related to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.
Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and nursing mothers.
(2) Public service providers are obliged to provide special facilities for nursing mothers.
Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
(2) Employers are obliged to place Women workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
(3) Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of Women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.
Article 20 (1) Women workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(3) Employers who employ Women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, are obliged to:
a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

DECIDES:
REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One
Definitions, Meanings and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency.
2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields.
11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights.
12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.
29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the government or community-based.

a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervising the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
(2) The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

(4) Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.

(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

25. WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
Article 52 (1) The Regency Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for Women.
(2) The implementation of Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and Community Organizations.
Article 53 (1) The Regency Government provides skills training to increase the capacity of Women.
(2) In providing training as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regency Government may cooperate with training institutions organized by community organizations.
(3) The Regency Government expands access and opportunities for Women in obtaining skills and employment.
Article 54 (1) The Regency Government facilitates:
a. provision of business capital assistance for Women with weak economies;
b. marketing of products resulting from Women's businesses;
c. implementation of training for community capacity development through economic empowerment of pre-prosperous families;
d. expansion of access, information and provision of knowledge to Women regarding marketing efforts for products produced; and e. provision of comprehensive entrepreneurship training to Women.
(2) The Regency Government in facilitating activities as referred to in paragraph (1) cooperates with the community and/or community organizations.

Paragraph 1
General Article 16 The Regency Government organizes the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of Women's protection.
Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters related to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.
Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and nursing mothers.
(2) Public service providers are obliged to provide special facilities for nursing mothers.
Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
(2) Employers are obliged to place Women workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
(3) Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of Women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.
Article 20 (1) Women workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(3) Employers who employ Women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, are obliged to:
a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.
Paragraph 5 Education

REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One
Definitions, Meanings and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency.
2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields.
11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights.
12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.
29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the government or community-based.

CHAPTER X
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts development and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
(2) Development as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. training for government apparatus and law enforcers regarding prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent in conducting development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.
Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obligated to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.
(2) The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
(2) The results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of Women and Children protection programs in the Regency.

Article 21
Women are guaranteed the right to obtain education at every level of formal and non-formal education.
Paragraph 6 Social Article 22 (1) The Regency Government shall organize empowerment of Women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability through productive economic business activities.
(2) Community Organizations may conduct empowerment for Women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability as referred to in paragraph (1) in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Paragraph 1
General Article 16 The Regency Government organizes the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of Women's protection.
Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters related to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.
Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and nursing mothers.
(2) Public service providers are obliged to provide special facilities for nursing mothers.
Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
(2) Employers are obliged to place Women workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
(3) Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of Women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.
Article 20 (1) Women workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(3) Employers who employ Women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, are obliged to:
a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.
Paragraph 5 Education

CHAPTER VII
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
Article 52 (1) The Regency Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for Women.
(2) The implementation of Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and Community Organizations.
Article 53 (1) The Regency Government provides skills training to increase the capacity of Women.
(2) In providing training as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regency Government may cooperate with training institutions organized by community organizations.
(3) The Regency Government expands access and opportunities for Women in obtaining skills and employment.
Article 54 (1) The Regency Government facilitates:
a. provision of business capital assistance for Women with weak economies;
b. marketing of products resulting from Women's businesses;
c. implementation of training for community capacity development through economic empowerment of pre-prosperous families;

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One
Definitions, Meanings and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency.
2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields.
11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights.
12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.
29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the government or community-based.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One
Definitions, Meanings and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency.
2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields.
11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights.
12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.
29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the government or community-based.

2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb.
9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields.
11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights.
12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.
29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the government or community-based.

Part Five
Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services Article 51 (1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.
(2) Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) The Regency Government shall implement repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Paragraph 1
Health Article 23 (1) The District Government's efforts to provide protection for Children in the health sector include: a. free health services for Children from poor families;
b. the provision of optimal health care for Children to obtain good health status from the womb;
c. ensuring that infants receive exclusive breastfeeding from their mothers properly and naturally;
d. ensuring Children receive adequate nutrition;
e. ensuring newborn Children undergo screening; and
f. ensuring the provision of growth and development monitoring for toddlers and pre-school age children.
(2) The District Government, families, and parents protect children from efforts to transplant their body organs to other parties.
Paragraph 2 Education Article 24 Children in formal and non-formal educational institution environments must be protected from acts of violence.
Article 25 Every Child aged 7 (seven) to 18 (eighteen) years who has not completed education, exceeding 3 (three) years beyond the age limit for formal education may pursue education through non-formal education units:
a. Package A equivalency program equivalent to Elementary School and Madrasah Ibtidaiyah;
b. Package B equivalency program equivalent to Junior High School and Madrasah Tsanawiyah; and
c. Package C equivalency program equivalent to Senior High School, Madrasah Aliyah and Vocational High School.
Article 26 (1) Children with special needs and/or who have potential intelligence and/or special talents are given equal opportunities and facilities to obtain regular education or inclusive education.
(2) Inclusive education as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized by the District Government and the community.
Article 27 Every organizer of formal education is prohibited from expelling Children without guarantees for the continuity of the Child's education.
Article 28 (1) The District Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:
a. children from poor families;
b. neglected children; and
c. children residing in remote areas.
(2) The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and community organizations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the provision of scholarships and or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.
Article 29 Children in conflict with the law, Child victims of violence and sexual abuse and Child victims of HIV/AIDS transmission are protected in their rights to obtain education.

Article 49 (1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services constitute actions by law enforcement officials provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.
(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
Article 50 (1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 49 are intended to provide accompaniment and protection to Women and Children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty of rights.
(2) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of BAP; b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.
(3) The Regency Government shall provide legal assistance to Children and Women victims of violence free of charge.
(4) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regency Government may cooperate with:
a. Legal Aid Institute (LBH);
b. Women Crisis Center (WCC);
c. Advocates; and/or
d. other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

CHAPTER X
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts development and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
(2) Development as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. training for government apparatus and law enforcers regarding prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent in conducting development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.
Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obligated to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.
(2) The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
(2) The results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of Women and Children protection programs in the Regency.

CHAPTER VII
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
Article 52 (1) The Regency Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for Women.
(2) The implementation of Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and Community Organizations.
Article 53 (1) The Regency Government provides skills training to increase the capacity of Women.
(2) In providing training as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regency Government may cooperate with training institutions organized by community organizations.
(3) The Regency Government expands access and opportunities for Women in obtaining skills and employment.
Article 54 (1) The Regency Government facilitates:
a. provision of business capital assistance for Women with weak economies;
b. marketing of products resulting from Women's businesses;
c. implementation of training for community capacity development through economic empowerment of pre-prosperous families;
d. expansion of access, information and provision of knowledge to Women regarding marketing efforts for products produced; and e. provision of comprehensive entrepreneurship training to Women.
(2) The Regency Government in facilitating activities as referred to in paragraph (1) cooperates with the community and/or community organizations.

Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters related to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.
Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and nursing mothers.
(2) Public service providers are obliged to provide special facilities for nursing mothers.
Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
(2) Employers are obliged to place Women workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
(3) Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of Women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.
Article 20 (1) Women workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts development and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
(2) Development as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. training for government apparatus and law enforcers regarding prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent in conducting development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.
Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obligated to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.
(2) The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
(2) The results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of Women and Children protection programs in the Regency.

Paragraph 1
Health Article 23 (1) The District Government's efforts to provide protection for Children in the health sector include: a. free health services for Children from poor families;
b. the provision of optimal health care for Children to obtain good health status from the womb;
c. ensuring that infants receive exclusive breastfeeding from their mothers properly and naturally;
d. ensuring Children receive adequate nutrition;
e. ensuring newborn Children undergo screening; and
f. ensuring the provision of growth and development monitoring for toddlers and pre-school age children.
(2) The District Government, families, and parents protect children from efforts to transplant their body organs to other parties.
Paragraph 2 Education Article 24 Children in formal and non-formal educational institution environments must be protected from acts of violence.
Article 25 Every Child aged 7 (seven) to 18 (eighteen) years who has not completed education, exceeding 3 (three) years beyond the age limit for formal education may pursue education through non-formal education units:
a. Package A equivalency program equivalent to Elementary School and Madrasah Ibtidaiyah;
b. Package B equivalency program equivalent to Junior High School and Madrasah Tsanawiyah; and
c. Package C equivalency program equivalent to Senior High School, Madrasah Aliyah and Vocational High School.
Article 26 (1) Children with special needs and/or who have potential intelligence and/or special talents are given equal opportunities and facilities to obtain regular education or inclusive education.
(2) Inclusive education as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized by the District Government and the community.
Article 27 Every organizer of formal education is prohibited from expelling Children without guarantees for the continuity of the Child's education.
Article 28 (1) The District Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:
a. children from poor families;
b. neglected children; and
c. children residing in remote areas.
(2) The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and community organizations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the provision of scholarships and or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.
Article 29 Children in conflict with the law, Child victims of violence and sexual abuse and Child victims of HIV/AIDS transmission are protected in their rights to obtain education.

7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields.
11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights.
12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.

17. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.

30. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the government or community-based.

Paragraph 1
Health Article 23 (1) The District Government's efforts to provide protection for Children in the health sector include: a. free health services for Children from poor families;
b. the provision of optimal health care for Children to obtain good health status from the womb;
c. ensuring that infants receive exclusive breastfeeding from their mothers properly and naturally;
d. ensuring Children receive adequate nutrition;
e. ensuring newborn Children undergo screening; and
f. ensuring the provision of growth and development monitoring for toddlers and pre-school age children.
(2) The District Government, families, and parents protect children from efforts to transplant their body organs to other parties.
Paragraph 2 Education Article 24 Children in formal and non-formal educational institution environments must be protected from acts of violence.
Article 25 Every Child aged 7 (seven) to 18 (eighteen) years who has not completed education, exceeding 3 (three) years beyond the age limit for formal education may pursue education through non-formal education units:
a. Package A equivalency program equivalent to Elementary School and Madrasah Ibtidaiyah;
b. Package B equivalency program equivalent to Junior High School and Madrasah Tsanawiyah; and
c. Package C equivalency program equivalent to Senior High School, Madrasah Aliyah and Vocational High School.
Article 26 (1) Children with special needs and/or who have potential intelligence and/or special talents are given equal opportunities and facilities to obtain regular education or inclusive education.
(2) Inclusive education as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized by the District Government and the community.
Article 27 Every organizer of formal education is prohibited from expelling Children without guarantees for the continuity of the Child's education.
Article 28 (1) The District Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:
a. children from poor families;
b. neglected children; and
c. children residing in remote areas.
(2) The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and community organizations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the provision of scholarships and or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.
Article 29 Children in conflict with the law, Child victims of violence and sexual abuse and Child victims of HIV/AIDS transmission are protected in their rights to obtain education.

Part Five
Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services Article 51 (1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.
(2) Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) The Regency Government shall implement repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

c. prevention of unregistered marriages/siri marriages. (2) Efforts undertaken in order to prevent violations of Children's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that give rise to violations of Children's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of marriage at the age of Children.

Paragraph 1
General Article 16 The Regency Government organizes the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of Women's protection.
Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters related to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.
Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and nursing mothers.
(2) Public service providers are obliged to provide special facilities for nursing mothers.
Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
(2) Employers are obliged to place Women workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
(3) Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of Women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.
Article 20 (1) Women workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
(3) Employers who employ Women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, are obliged to:
a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.
Paragraph 5 Education
